newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes drive higher on cold weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes drive higher on cold weather concerns.

text.p: U.S. crude oil prices ended at lofty levels Monday, rocketing higher on weather forecasts calling for extreme cold temperatures across large sections of the United States.

Even as many players scratched their heads at the prospects for $26.00 a barrel spot crude, the market remained buoyant to the close, focused squarely on calls for Arctic cold spells for the Midwest, Northeast and Southern U.S.
January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing settled $1.25 higher at $25.70-80 a barrel. NYMEX gains approached new post-Gulf War highs, trading as high as $25.95 a barrel.
